constraints.description: [R-1, AC-1, A-1] Add `round_number` to the existing module `src/app_int/main.py`. Do not create a new module and do not edit `src/app_int/__init__.py`.
[R-2, AC-14, N-1] The signature must be exactly `round_number(value: int | float, ndigits: int = 0) -> int | float`. Both parameters and the return value must have annotations.
[N-2, AC-15] Use only the standard library (`decimal`, `math`). Do not modify `pyproject.toml`, including the empty `dependencies` list.
[R-6, AC-5, AC-6] Round with `decimal.ROUND_HALF_UP` (half away from zero). Do not use the built-in `round()` for the rounding step, and do not use ROUND_HALF_EVEN or ROUND_HALF_DOWN.
[R-7, AC-7] Convert float input to Decimal from its shortest representation (`repr`/`str`), never with `Decimal(float)` directly. Convert int input with `Decimal(int)`.
[R-8, AC-8, AC-9] Return `int` when `ndigits <= 0` and `float` when `ndigits > 0`, whatever the input type.

[R-10, R-11, AC-10, AC-11] Raise `TypeError` when `value` is a bool or not an int/float, and when `ndigits` is a bool or not an int. Check bool explicitly before the int check. Validate in this order: value type, then ndigits type, then finiteness.
[R-12, AC-12] Raise `ValueError` for NaN, +inf and -inf `value`. Check with `math.isfinite` after the type checks.

[R-13, AC-13] The function must be pure: no print or logging, no I/O, no module-level caches. Any decimal precision change must use a scoped `decimal.localcontext()`. Never mutate `decimal.getcontext()` globally.

[Design decision] Set the quantize precision high enough that large ints, large floats or large positive `ndigits` never raise `decimal.InvalidOperation`. Use a local context with prec >= max(28, integer digits of the value + max(ndigits, 0) + margin).
[N-1, AC-14] The docstring must be non-empty and contain the literal phrase "half away from zero". It should also describe the return-type rule, negative `ndigits`, and the exceptions raised.
[Write scope] DEVELOPMENT edits only under `src/**`. Tests for `round_number` (AC-18) are written by QA under `tests/**`, e.g. a new `tests/test_round_number.py`.

[N-4, AC-17] `uv run pytest -q` and `uv run ruff check .` must both exit 0. Imports must satisfy Ruff rules E, F, I, UP and B: stdlib imports after `from __future__ import annotations`, isort-ordered, and lines no longer than 100 characters.
